- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

1	# Architecture
2	
3	*Key technical decisions, stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths. Update this file when the stack changes, a new integration is added, or a structural decision is made.*
4	
5	Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com — multi-locale, multi-currency, seven storefronts across six regions (AU, US, UK, EU, HK, ME), with the EU as two storefronts (domestic + international).
6	
7	## Pre-Build Decisions
8	
9	These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.
10	
11	| # | Decision | Status |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| 1 | Browser & device matrix | ✅ Confirmed (informal) |
14	| 2 | Accessibility manual testing | 🟡 Partial — vendor info pending |
15	| 3 | Performance budgets | ✅ Confirmed (informal) |
16	| 4 | Client-side error reporting | ⚪ Accepted risk — no tool |
17	| 5 | Feature-flag tool | ⚪ Accepted risk — Optimizely Web only |
18	| 6 | Translation fallback chain | 🟡 Partial — Brand/Legal pending |
19	
20	### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅
21	**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
22	**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.
23	
24	### #2 — Accessibility 🟡
25	**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
26	**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.
27	
28	### #3 — Performance budgets ✅
29	**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
30	**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
31	**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
32	**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
33	**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. As of the last measurement the actual sizes are well above these ceilings (`main.js` ~352 kB, `vendor.js` ~2 MB) before any optimisation pass — the ceilings need to be re-baselined against measured size + a growth-only headroom (e.g. current + 10–15%) once a baseline pass is done.) Their purpose is regression detection, not a client-facing commitment.
34	**Third-party script weight:** uncapped — tight LCP is the de-facto constraint. See AGENTS.md > Performance for the deferral rule.
35	
36	### #6 — Translation fallback 🟡
37	[regional.md](./prd/regional.md) REG-046: "English is the site-wide fallback." Doesn't disambiguate `en-eu` vs `en`, nor split by content type.
38	**Pending Brand/Legal decision** on the rule per content type:
39	
40	| Content type | Suggested chain | Why |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| UI strings | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → `en` | Universal meaning |
43	| Editorial | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Avoid half-translated pages |
44	| Product copy | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Care/sizing are region-specific (regulatory) |
45	
46	REG-047 (Contentful↔Transperfect↔SFCC workflow) remains separately TBC.
47	
48	### Accepted risks
49	
50	**#4 — No client-side error reporting.** JS errors in customer browsers (e.g. Adyen iframe failure on a specific iOS Safari version) are invisible to the team; detection relies on support tickets. Revisit post-launch if checkout completion dips unexplained.
51	
52	**#5 — No feature-flag tool.** Optimizely Web Experimentation ([analytics.md](./prd/analytics.md) AAB-004) covers analytics A/B. Note (confirmed 09-06): Optimizely is **not** a GTM tag — the PWA loads its script directly in the page head (US storefront only, single snippet across environments, before render to avoid flicker), Didomi-gated. Progressive rollout, social login dark-launch, and August-2026 payment-method gating will be handled via deploy timing and branch merges — no instant kill-switch, no % rollouts.
53	
54	## Frontend Stack
55	
56	### Bundled by PWA Kit
57	| Layer | Library | Notes |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| Base framework | PWA Kit v3+ | Salesforce storefront foundation |

228	## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope
229	All seven storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.

234	## Blast-Radius Mitigation
235	
236	Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
237	
238	The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
239	
240	```ts
241	import { Pool } from 'undici'
242	
243	// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
244	const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
245	  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
246	  timeout: 8000
247	})
248	
249	// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
250	async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
251	  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
252	    dispatcher: checkoutPool // Safely isolated!
253	  })
254	}
255	```

# Architecture

*Key technical decisions, stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths. Update this file when the stack changes, a new integration is added, or a structural decision is made.*

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com — multi-locale, multi-currency, seven storefronts across six regions (AU, US, UK, EU, HK, ME), with the EU as two storefronts (domestic + international).

## Pre-Build Decisions

These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.

| # | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Browser & device matrix | ✅ Confirmed (informal) |
| 2 | Accessibility manual testing | 🟡 Partial — vendor info pending |
| 3 | Performance budgets | ✅ Confirmed (informal) |
| 4 | Client-side error reporting | ⚪ Accepted risk — no tool |
| 5 | Feature-flag tool | ⚪ Accepted risk — Optimizely Web only |
| 6 | Translation fallback chain | 🟡 Partial — Brand/Legal pending |

### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅
**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.

### #2 — Accessibility 🟡
**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.

### #3 — Performance budgets ✅
**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. As of the last measurement the actual sizes are well above these ceilings (`main.js` ~352 kB, `vendor.js` ~2 MB) before any optimisation pass — the ceilings need to be re-baselined against measured size + a growth-only headroom (e.g. current + 10–15%) once a baseline pass is done.) Their purpose is regression detection, not a client-facing commitment.
**Third-party script weight:** uncapped — tight LCP is the de-facto constraint. See AGENTS.md > Performance for the deferral rule.

### #6 — Translation fallback 🟡
[regional.md](./prd/regional.md) REG-046: "English is the site-wide fallback." Doesn't disambiguate `en-eu` vs `en`, nor split by content type.
**Pending Brand/Legal decision** on the rule per content type:

| Content type | Suggested chain | Why |
|---|---|---|
| UI strings | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → `en` | Universal meaning |
| Editorial | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Avoid half-translated pages |
| Product copy | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Care/sizing are region-specific (regulatory) |

REG-047 (Contentful↔Transperfect↔SFCC workflow) remains separately TBC.

### Accepted risks

**#4 — No client-side error reporting.** JS errors in customer browsers (e.g. Adyen iframe failure on a specific iOS Safari version) are invisible to the team; detection relies on support tickets. Revisit post-launch if checkout completion dips unexplained.

**#5 — No feature-flag tool.** Optimizely Web Experimentation ([analytics.md](./prd/analytics.md) AAB-004) covers analytics A/B. Note (confirmed 09-06): Optimizely is **not** a GTM tag — the PWA loads its script directly in the page head (US storefront only, single snippet across environments, before render to avoid flicker), Didomi-gated. Progressive rollout, social login dark-launch, and August-2026 payment-method gating will be handled via deploy timing and branch merges — no instant kill-switch, no % rollouts.

## Frontend Stack

### Bundled by PWA Kit
| Layer | Library | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Base framework | PWA Kit v3+ | Salesforce storefront foundation |
| UI framework | React 18 + Chakra UI | Component library + theme system |
| Routing | React Router v6 | |
| Server/async state | TanStack Query (via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) | All SFCC data fetching |
| i18n | react-intl | Translations in `translations/` |
| Build + dev server | Webpack 5 (via `pwa-kit-dev`) | |
| Build + test runner (legacy) | Jest (via `pwa-kit-dev test`) | `jest.config.js` — kept for PWA Kit internals; superseded by Vitest for project tests |

### Project additions
| Layer | Library | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Type safety | TypeScript strict mode | `tsconfig.json` |
| Component explorer + interaction tests | Storybook 8 | `storybook dev -p 6006`; `play` functions are the primary tool for component-level interaction testing |
| Storybook a11y addon | `@storybook/addon-a11y` | Component-level accessibility checks during development and in Storybook test runs |
| Unit test runner | Vitest | `vitest.config.ts`; replaces `pwa-kit-dev test` for project tests |
| Accessibility testing | axe-core (via `vitest-axe` / `axe-playwright`) | Automated WCAG checks in unit and E2E layers; see Pre-Build Decisions #2 for outstanding items |
| E2E tests (planned) | Playwright | Not yet configured |
| Forms + validation | react-hook-form + zod | Not yet installed; add when checkout/account work begins |
| Global UI state | Zustand | For shared state that outgrows Context (multi-step flows, drawer state, etc.). **SSR note:** initialise store per-request — never as a module singleton — to prevent state leaking across server-rendered requests. |

### External services
Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Contentful Studio CMS, Global-e (international checkout + server-side pricing/catalogue feed — PRC-34..43 sign-off pending), Didomi (consent), GTM hosted on Addingwell (data layer + downstream tag loading via Tell No Lies). Full integration map below.

## Environments

Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |

**Stage** is the contractual performance-test environment referenced under [Pre-Build Decisions #3](#3--performance-budgets-) — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

**QA workflow** ([`qa.yml`](../.github/workflows/qa.yml)) runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`: Vitest unit tests and Storybook interaction + `@storybook/addon-a11y` component-level accessibility checks (`storybook test --ci`), in parallel. Code-correctness checks that run before any environment is involved.

**SIT gate** ([`digital-sit.yml`](../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)) runs on push/PR to `release/**`: Playwright `p0` specs, bundle-size check, MuleSoft contract tests, Lighthouse CI thresholds, LHCI trend gate. Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier. On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev. Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.

**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`. `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | stage | uat | prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry, New Relic, and GTM.

## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.

## Overrides Pattern
All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.

**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.

**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**

## New vs. Override Components
- **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/` (see Overrides Pattern above).
- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.

## Key Paths
- **Country/locale/currency mappings:** `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — single source of truth for URL slugs, locales, currencies, shipping countries, Global-e flag, and boutique regions. When adding a market also update `config/sites.js`.
- **Contentful config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — always render locale-specific content using Contentful's native localisation fields. Gate preview/draft content behind a server-side check; never expose draft content in production.
- **Theme / design tokens:** `overrides/app/theme/` — `index.ts` composes the theme; brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); per-component overrides live one file each in `components/` (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — Tier 2). Register a new component override in `components/index.ts`.
- **App shell (Header/Footer):** `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`
- **Header:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`
- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/`
- **Assets:** `overrides/app/static/`, `overrides/app/assets/svg/`

## Design Source of Truth
Figma file "29 April 2026" is the **current working draft** — not a signed-off final design. Implementations based on it are client-preview builds and may need to be revised when designs are finalised. Do not treat any Figma-derived decision as confirmed without explicit sign-off.

Desktop prototype at zimm-prototype.vercel.app is AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design.

## Header Layout (based on draft Figma, subject to change)
Two rows: top bar (nav + icons) and logo row. Implemented in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, with Chakra theme overrides split across `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts`.

**Logo**: uses `BrandLogo` from the icons package (PWA default with the svg file replaced). The Z.IMMERSE variant has not been implemented yet.

**ListMenu active-state gotcha**: `listMenuTriggerLinkActive` is JS-spread *after* `listMenuTriggerLink` on the same `<Link>` element. Any `_after` key in the active style entirely replaces the base `_after` object — all CSS properties must be repeated, not just the overriding ones.

**Icons deferred**: Boutique, Contact, Newsletter (HPC-015) — icon assets not provided yet.

**Base functionality retained**: All hooks, the account popover, wishlist, store locator, and all existing props are unchanged. Only layout and visual style changed so far.

## Contentful Content Type Management

Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are defined in code and synced via a script. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and team-safe.

**Key paths:**
- `scripts/contentful/sync.js` — runner: upserts (creates or updates) and publishes every content type in the definitions directory
- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `shoppableImage.js`)

**To register a new content type:**
1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`

**To run the sync:**
```
npm run sync:contentful
```
Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` in `.env` at the repo root (never commit). Get it from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` and `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` are already in `.env`.

The script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It preserves any existing fields not in the definition file (it will not delete fields from a live content type).

**Relationship to the React component:**
Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.

**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding `sync:contentful` entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

## Path Aliases
Configured in four places (keep in sync):
- `babel.config.js` — `babel-plugin-module-resolver` (covers `npm start` dev server + `npm run build`)
- `tsconfig.json` — `baseUrl` + `paths` (TypeScript / VS Code intellisense)
- `.storybook/main.js` — `webpackFinal` alias
- `jest.config.js` — `moduleNameMapper` (PWA Kit internals)
- `vitest.config.ts` — `resolve.alias` (project tests)

| Alias | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| `~` | project root |
| `app` | `overrides/app` |

## Integration Map

All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly for read operations (order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, real-time stock availability, GiveX balance check) — SFCC is not in those read paths. A handful of services are also called **browser-direct from the PWA** and another set are **SFCC cartridge integrations** invoked server-side. The `Boundary` column makes this explicit so you know where to look when an integration breaks.

**Boundary key:**
- **PWA-direct** — called from the browser directly. Vendor key (if any) is publishable/public and safe in the bundle.
- **MRT-mediated** — called from the PWA's Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` or a server-only endpoint. API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. Includes direct PWA → MuleSoft calls via MRT proxy.
- **SFCC (OOTB)** — Salesforce-bundled integration; no custom cartridge.
- **SFCC (cartridge)** — vendor-supplied or custom server-side cartridge running inside SFCC.
- **SFCC → MuleSoft** — SFCC calls MuleSoft, which fans out to the downstream system.
- **Browser handoff** — PWA hands the user off to a third party's hosted experience.
- **Out-of-band** — no runtime call from PWA or SFCC; the integration delivers data via a separate channel.

| System | Role | Boundary | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC)** | Storefront, product catalogue, order management (record of truth), customer accounts, Business Manager config | — | Domestic checkout owner |
| **MuleSoft** | Middleware / integration layer | SFCC → MuleSoft + MRT-mediated (direct PWA → MuleSoft calls) | All SFCC ↔ OMS, SFCC ↔ Omneo, SFCC ↔ Narvar calls go via MuleSoft. Select PWA operations also call MuleSoft directly via the MRT proxy layer (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) with credentials held as MRT environment variables |
| **NewStore OMS** | Order management system, carrier selection, dispatch, label generation, boutique inventory; **system of record for order history** (no Magento order history is migrated — DMU-007/008) | SFCC → MuleSoft (writes) + MRT-mediated (reads) | **Write path (SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore):** order creation, fulfilment, BOPIS. **Read path (MRT → MuleSoft → NewStore):** order history (CRM-056–057), order details (CRM-071–072), boutique / BOPIS stock check (CFD-043), real-time stock availability. SFCC is not in the read path. The customer-identification mechanism on the read path is **unconfirmed** (open item) — either MRT forwards the customer's SLAS JWT for MuleSoft to validate, or MRT passes the customer ID as a request parameter; whichever is agreed must prevent retrieval of an arbitrary customer's data |
| **AP21** | Retail Rewards (loyalty/VIP), product master, composition/material data; **source of product and pricing master data** | SFCC → MuleSoft | Real-time AP21 call at login for Retail Rewards balance; used for HS codes via Avalara. **Product and pricing feed** flows inbound AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC to populate the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks the PWA reads via SCAPI; feed cadence and exact field set TBC. |
| **Omneo** | CRM sync layer / system of record for customer identity and loyalty | SFCC → MuleSoft | SFCC ↔ Omneo via MuleSoft; Omneo → Emarsys for marketing emails |
| **Emarsys** | Email marketing platform | Out-of-band | Receives opt-in/opt-out from Omneo; sends welcome and marketing emails |

Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna targeting August 2026. Adyen Web Drop-in loads in the browser at checkout for tokenisation and 3DS2 challenges. As payment processing is strictly necessary (contractual necessity, not analytics/marketing tracking), the Drop-in is **not** Didomi consent-gated — it loads at the payment step regardless of consent choices. | **Global-e** | International checkout owner (HK, ME, all international orders) + server-side pricing/catalogue feed into SFCC | PWA-direct (iframe embed at checkout) + SFCC server-side (pricing/catalogue feed) | (1) **Iframe embed at checkout** — Global-e hosted checkout renders inside an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route (not a full-page redirect). SFCC sends complete cart in target currency at handoff. CSP `frame-src` must allowlist the Global-e origin. (2) Server-side feed — nightly FX rates / coefficients / rounding rules from Global-e generate Global-e-market pricebooks in SFCC (PRC-34..43); daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue CSV via SFTP (PRC-54); GiveX validate/redeem/refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44). REG-041 confirmed; PRC-34..43 final sign-off pending. |
| **Booxi** | Boutique appointment booking (My Account → appointment history; CRM-165–167) | MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi) | **Not a MuleSoft path** — the PWA calls Booxi directly from the MRT Node layer; SFCC and MuleSoft are not involved. Booxi credentials held as MRT environment variables. Previously referred to as "Booksy" in older notes — Booxi is the correct vendor. Scope still TBC. |
| **Narvar** | EDD at checkout (Promise widget, formerly CONVERT), domestic order confirmation emails, shipping confirmation, tracking portal, returns portal | SFCC → MuleSoft (backend); PWA-direct (Promise widget) | Narvar is NOT used for international orders (Global-e owns those) |
| **Contentful** | CMS for editorial/homepage content, size guides, promotional banners | PWA-direct (CDA) + MRT-mediated (CPA preview, publish webhook) | Contentful Studio with live preview; locale-specific content via Contentful native localisation. Cache invalidation on entry publish via a Contentful → MRT webhook, HMAC-verified with `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. |

Didomi-gated (Analytics). SFCC populates the data-layer segmentation attributes (authenticated state, customer group, loyalty status, storefront region, new vs returning, device type) per AAB-002. |
| **Crazy Egg** | Heatmapping & session replay (AAB-005) | PWA-direct front-end head tag (post-consent) | **Not a GTM tag.** PWA loads the Crazy Egg snippet directly in the page head — **async and post-Didomi-consent**, so it never blocks first paint (no anti-flicker exemption, unlike Optimizely). Didomi-gated (Analytics). SFCC populates data-layer attributes (page type, authenticated state, storefront region) per AAB-002. |
| **Avalara** | Tax calculation for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic | SFCC (cartridge) | EU domestic added 2026-06-19 (Third_Party_Integrations sheet update). UK uses SFCC native VAT tables; all other storefronts use SFCC native tax tables. |

MRT exposes an HTTPS balance-check endpoint that proxies to MuleSoft and returns a typed JSON response to the PWA. The balance-check request carries the card number **and PIN** (secure PINs enabled — both payment credentials, POST body only, never logged). Checkout redemption flows server-side (PWA → SCAPI/SFCC → NewStore adapter → GiveX) as a SCAPI payment instrument, not through the PWA directly. **Gift card purchase** is a PWA-rendered surface: physical and digital products (separate product IDs), fixed denominations ($100/$200/$250/$300/$500), and a sender / recipient / recipient-email / delivery-date / optional-message form; the PWA persists these as basket line-item attributes, and issuance (E-Cert Order for digital, Activate for physical) is server-side via SCAPI/SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX. Separate from AP21 Retail Rewards — both can be used in a single checkout |
| **Transperfect** | Translation pipeline (for Contentful content) | Out-of-band | Translated copy lands in Contentful via vendor workflow. Translation workflow trigger TBD |
| **Inside Chat** | Customer support chat widget | Loaded by GTM / Addingwell (post-consent) | **Loaded via GTM script injection through the Addingwell container, not a direct PWA include** (HPC-039/040). Initialised only after Didomi consent; shown on relevant pages per Inside Chat rules |
| **Zendesk** | Customer service ticketing — hosts the public "Contact Us" form | Out-of-band (external link) | **Not an embedded integration.** The PWA's "Contact Us" CTA links out to the Zendesk-hosted form on a Zendesk domain — no iframe, no SDK, no API call from the PWA. | **Google reCAPTCHA** | Bot protection on registration/login | Browser-direct (site key) + MRT-mediated (token verification) | Site key public in bundle (`RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`); secret key held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable — MRT verifies the token via Google's `siteverify` endpoint before forwarding to SCAPI; the secret key never reaches the browser. Loads on register/login **form interaction**. **Consent-gated in EU & UK only** (loads only post-Didomi-consent, so a visitor who declines is not challenged and there's no bot protection there); elsewhere it loads regardless of consent. |
| **GDPR cartridge** | DSAR export, right-to-erasure, configurable retention | SFCC (cartridge) | Replaces manual legal/IT ticketing. PWA-side touchpoints: localised privacy policy pages (from Contentful), the consent UI itself (Didomi), and surfacing the customer-initiated erasure / export trigger in My Account where exposed by SFCC. Full requirements: REG-060–067. |
| **Shippit / Ordoro** | Carrier label automation | OMS-level only | SFCC passes address to MuleSoft, not directly to these |
| **Google Business API** | Store hours feed (boutique opening hours) | Out-of-band (daily feed into SFCC) | Consumed by Find in Boutique / store-locator UI — PWA renders, does not call Google directly |
| **Feedonomics** | Product feed for downstream marketing channels (PRD-071) | Out-of-band | No PWA runtime touchpoint; flagged for SEO/marketing dependency awareness only |
| **Measmerize** | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP (PRD-050–053) | PWA-direct (script injection on PDP only) | Browser-direct; no MRT proxy. Script injected once on PDP mount; widget self-determines product availability and signals the PWA via events. Falls back to the Contentful size guide when Measmerize has no data for the product. **Consent approach unconfirmed — open item.** Implementation detail: [.docs/temp/integration/17-measmerize.md](.docs/temp/integration/17-measmerize.md). Vendor SDK reference: [.docs/vendor/measmerize.md](.docs/vendor/measmerize.md). |

## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope
All seven storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.

## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.

## Blast-Radius Mitigation

Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.

The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

```ts
import { Pool } from 'undici'

// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
  timeout: 8000
})

// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
    dispatcher: checkoutPool // Safely isolated!
  })
}
```

The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):

| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sfcc-scapi` | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com` | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |
| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com` | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
| `google-places` | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |

## Zimmermann PWA — Codebase Summary

### Project Identity

- **Framework:** Salesforce PWA Kit v3+ extending `@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`
- **Extensibility model:** `ccExtensibility.extends` + `overridesDir: "overrides"` — all Zimmermann code lives exclusively inside `overrides/`
- **TypeScript:** Strict mode, no-emit, Babel handles transpilation. All `overrides/` files must be `.ts`/`.tsx`
- **Phase:** Sprint 0 foundation complete, Sprint 1 started (29 Jun – 10 Jul 2026). No production build yet beyond scaffolding.

---

### 1. Root Directory Structure

```
.browserstack.yml       — BrowserStack Automate config (iOS 17+, Android 14+, desktop matrix)
.claude/                — Claude Code rules, registry, hooks, skills
.docs/                  — Architecture docs, PRDs, memory files, integration specs
.eslintrc.js / .prettierrc.yaml / babel.config.js
.github/workflows/      — 10 CI/CD workflow files (see CI section)
.husky/                 — Git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg)
.storybook/             — Storybook 10 with React-Webpack5, a11y addon, babel compiler
config/                 — Tier 1. default.js, sites.js, dev.js, sit.js, stg.js, uat.js, production.js, utils.js
e2e/                    — Playwright E2E (gherkin-first approach)
jest.config.js          — Extends @salesforce/pwa-kit-dev Jest config; path aliases wired
kilo.json               — Contentful MCP server config (OAuth via kilo.ai)
overrides/              — All Zimmermann customisation (mirrors retail-react-app structure)
package.json            — v0.0.1, Node 18/20/22/24, npm 9/10/11
scripts/                — Contentful sync, registry generation, cursor rules sync, release tooling
translations/           — 26 locale JSON files (AU en, US, UK, EU/FR/IT/ES, HK, ME, AE, CH + extras)
tsconfig.json           — Strict, noEmit, paths: `~` → root, `app` → overrides/app
vitest.config.ts        — Vitest 3 (jsdom, @vitejs/plugin-react, same path aliases)
worker/main.js          — Tier 1. Service worker
```

config/

  countries.ts            — Tier 1. COUNTRIES record — 11 entries covering AU, US, en-ca, UK, en-eu/fr-eu/it-eu/es-eu, en-ch, hk, en-ae. Types: SfccSiteId, CheckoutOwner ('sfcc'|'global-e'|'hybrid'), CountryConfig
